archetype: Mardu Vampire ARISTOCRATS — an aggro shell (37 creature copies) whose bodies are fodder and fuel rather than the kill. v1.0.1 (decklist sha 7ce22fd6…, sleeved 2026-09-01) stopped asking Edgar's tokens to connect and started asking them to DIE. Edgar Markov's eminence still mints a 1/1 Vampire on every Vampire spell cast from the command zone, and three replacement doublers — Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer — multiply the mint (checker-passed stack 002: one {B}{B} cast becomes four tokens through two doublers; stack 010: eight through three). Nine sacrifice outlets by role (Altar of Dementia, Ashnod's Altar, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Immersturm Predator, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites, Viscera Seer, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter, Yahenni, Undying Partisan) convert those bodies into cards, +1/+1 counters and life loss at every seat. Both checker-passed kill routes are drains that need no combat damage to land: Sanctum Seeker's attack trigger doubled by Bloodletter of Aclazotz (stack 003) and Bloodthirsty Conqueror paired with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond (stacks 004 and 006, the deck's two contained two-card infinites). The combat layer is a small number of enormous Vampires — Cordial Vampire puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire each time any creature dies, and Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain, Captivating Vampire and Vampire Socialite stack statics — not an army of medium ones. This frame replaces the go-wide, entry-damage frame: the pilot's captain's log entry 003 (2026-08-28) withdrew that direction in as many words, and every entry-damage payoff the old frame named has been cut from the 99.

role_assignment.default_role: BEATDOWN, but by drain rather than by clock, and assigned per seat. Roles are 'set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label', and in a pod 'role is seat-relative — you can be the beatdown against one opponent and the control against another in the same turn cycle; assign per-threat, not per-game'. Two measurements say your clock is NOT fast and you should stop piloting as if it were: Forge, 100 games against the standard pod on this exact list (2026-09-02, seed base 1121742080), puts your MEDIAN FIRST ATTACK at global turn 13 (mean 14.97, n=92) — global turn is the GAME's turn counter, which in that run averaged 38.8 against a mean winner's round of 19.7, so turn 13 is roughly your own turn 6-7 and your win rate at 14/100, 0.144 with a 95% interval of [0.088, 0.228]; the goldfish (seed 42, 10,000 games, model 7054a07d1a47) kills a single unblocked opponent by turn 8 at the median, and it has no blockers at all. So the metagame-clock correction applies to you as a warning, not a licence — 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan and aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives'. What compresses here is not the attack: it is the drain, and the drain does not care who blocks.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Concrete events, per strategy:pivot-point — 'The pivot is usually triggered by a concrete event — a resolved engine, a wrath, a key removal spell spent, a life total crossing a clock threshold'. This deck's three: (1) a free outlet plus a death payoff both on the battlefield — an outlet is drawn in 77.6% of goldfish games (64.6% by turn 6, mean turn 3.04) and a death drain in 37.2% (24.7% by turn 6), and NOTHING measures the pair, so the trigger is the board, not the rate; (2) Bloodletter of Aclazotz resolving with Sanctum Seeker already out, which is the fastest verified kill (stack 003); (3) Bloodthirsty Conqueror resolving with Vito or Sanguine Bond, which ends the game at zero extra mana (stacks 004, 006). Take the window only when the attempt is one the table cannot profitably answer: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing'. Hold the free protection for that turn — 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after' — and note that Deflecting Swat, Flawless Maneuver, Teferi's Protection, Boros Charm and Akroma's Will are exactly what makes the commitment survivable.

engines.engine: Eminence: every Vampire spell you cast mints a 1/1 Vampire token from the command zone, so the ignition is free, undrawable and un-removable. What changed in v1.0.1 is the token's JOB — it is now sacrifice fodder and a draw trigger, not a member of a lethal attack. A castable Vampire is drawn in 95.1% of goldfish games at mean turn 2.19; Edgar himself is cast by turn 6 in 60.1% (median turn 6), and the deck does not need him on the battlefield.
engines.evidence: oracle text + verified stacks 002 and 010 (eminence resolves from the command zone; stack 010 re-proves it with Edgar never cast) + goldfish seed 42

engines.engine: Token multiplication, with Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer: three replacement doublers stack multiplicatively on every mint — 1→2→4 with two, 1→2→4→8 with three, identical for all six application orders. Multiplying FODDER is a different proposition from multiplying attackers: what the extra bodies buy now is outlet activations, death triggers and draw. A multiplier or extra token-maker is drawn in 67.3% of games (51.3% by turn 6).

The conversion layer, with Ashnod's Altar, Altar of Dementia, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Immersturm Predator, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter and Yahenni, Undying Partisan — nine sacrifice outlets by role, three of them free (Viscera Seer, Ashnod's Altar, Altar of Dementia). This is the whole of what v1.0.1 bought and it is the LEAST measured stage in the deck: a free outlet is drawn in 77.6% of goldfish games, but no artifact measures an outlet and a payoff together, and Forge's own AI activated the seat's abilities a mean of 2.63 times per game (median 2), which the bench has previously shown is a floor rather than a reading on a sacrifice deck.
engines.evidence: deck-facts roles (sac-outlet 9, sac-cost 9) + oracle text + goldfish target 0.776 + sim 2026-09-02 activations mean 2.63 [1.99, 3.27]

engines.engine: Deaths into SIZE: whenever any creature dies, each of your Vampires gets a +1/+1 counter. This is the mechanical answer to the 400-game finding that 1/1 tokens do not connect — the deck buys a few large bodies with deaths instead of many medium ones with tokens. It is the largest role class in the deck (buff:counters, 15 copies) and it composes with Indulgent Aristocrat's activated board-wide counter, Vampire Socialite's entry counters, Edgar's attack trigger and the four static lords.
engines.evidence: oracle text + deck-facts roles (buff:counters 15) + captain's log 003

engines.engine: Deaths and entries into CARDS — the dig engine the pivot asked for, with High-Society Hunter (another nontoken creature dies: draw), Liliana, Dreadhorde General (a creature you own dies: draw), Skullclamp (equipped creature dies: draw two), Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent (entries, both capped at once per turn), plus Champion of Dusk, Bloodtracker, Preacher of the Schism, Night's Whisper, Castle Locthwain and Minas Tirith. A draw engine is drawn in 84.1% of games at mean turn 2.68 — the healthiest component in the brief, and the direct fix for the 'ran out of steam' cause code on log entries 002 and 003. READ THE CAPS: Crossway Troublemakers sees Vampire deaths only and bills 2 life a card; High-Society Hunter's clause says 'another NONTOKEN creature', so it is blind to eminence tokens.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 0.841 (16 cards that draw, only 3 of them modelled — the other 13 are named in goldfish_metrics.meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled)

engines.engine: Death drain, with Cruel Celebrant. The asymmetry is not interchangeable and decides which one you play first: Blood Artist drains ONE TARGET PLAYER per death, Cruel Celebrant drains EACH OPPONENT — three-to-one in a pod. Together they are a two-card component assembled in 37.2% of goldfish games (24.7% by turn 6), the thinnest of the deck's engine components.

Attack drain, doubled by Bloodletter of Aclazotz: seven attacking Vampires make seven triggers, each drain doubled to 2 per opponent = 14 a seat, and the 14-life seat dies on the seventh trigger BEFORE BLOCKERS. This is the fastest verified kill in the deck and it is why width still matters even though the attack does not have to connect. Bloodletter's {1}{B}{B}{B} is the only cost in the 99 with three identical coloured pips, and Master of Dark Rites' restricted {B}{B}{B} can pay for it (Bloodletter is a Vampire Demon) — but not for any activated ability.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 + deck-facts mana.restricted_mana (Master of Dark Rites, spells_only) + goldfish drain-doubler target 0.042 assembled, 0.096 with the tutor

engines.engine: The two contained infinites, with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond: any lifegain starts a lifegain/lifeloss loop that kills the table at zero additional mana. BOTH lines rest on this ONE body — 7.6% assembled unassisted, 14.6% with Vampiric Tutor, 3.0% by turn 6 — which is the declared ceiling on the route, not a defect. The deck feeds it honestly: seven printed-lifelink bodies (Gifted Aetherborn, Indulgent Aristocrat, Nighthawk Scavenger, The Haunt of Hightower, Vampire Cutthroat, Vampire of the Dire Moon, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter), four makers of 1/1 lifelink Vampire tokens (Charismatic Conqueror, Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort, Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle, Preacher of the Schism) and three granters (Akroma's Will, Crossway Troublemakers, Vito's own {3}{B}{B}).
engines.evidence: combo_details (both lines contained, infinite, mana_value_needed 0, popularity 64,824 and 54,630) + verified stacks 004 and 006 + goldfish target 0.076/0.146

candidate_missing_lines.title: The v1.0.1 engine in one board: sacrifice N eminence tokens to a free outlet with Crossway Troublemakers and High-Society Hunter out — how many cards, at what life cost, and does the Hunter see any of them?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: Crossway Troublemakers reads 'Whenever a Vampire you control dies, you may pay 2 life. If you do, draw a card' and the eminence token is a black Vampire; High-Society Hunter reads 'Whenever another NONTOKEN creature dies, draw a card', which on a plain read is blind to every token the engine produces. This is the loop the pilot actually ran on 2026-09-01 (log 004) and it is the deck's central stage-to-stage arrow with no passing stack behind it. Whether the 2-life payment can be declined per trigger sets the real cap.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Altar of Dementia as a second kill: sacrifice a Vish Kal or a Haunt of Hightower grown by Cordial Vampire — is milling a seat out a real route in this 99, and what does the death pay on the way?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Altar of Dementia mills equal to the sacrificed creature's POWER, and this deck's power lives in +1/+1 counters: Vish Kal takes X counters equal to each sacrificed creature's power, Cordial Vampire adds one to every Vampire per death. A stack should settle the exact accounting — the order of Vish Kal's own sacrifice trigger against Cordial Vampire's, whether the drains fire for each death in the chain, and when the milled player actually loses (draw from an empty library is a state-based action on their next draw, not on the mill). It matters because it is the only alternate route in the deck and the one the 28-August pivot asked for.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Vampire Socialite's sequencing rule: cast the Vampire before or after the turn's first drain?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Socialite reads 'As long as an opponent lost life this turn, each other Vampire you control enters with an additional +1/+1 counter on it' — a free two power per token on the deck's most common turn, decided entirely by play order. Tracked stacks 002 and 011 record eminence tokens entering WITH and WITHOUT that counter on boards that differ only in timing, so the practical rule is unsettled and worth one scenario.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The wipe is now your engine, not your disaster. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says 'assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain' and to 'buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves'. v1.0.1 buys all three clauses: the death payoffs (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, Crossway Troublemakers, High-Society Hunter, Liliana, Dreadhorde General, Skullclamp) mean a resolved sweeper DRAINS the table and REFILLS your hand as the board dies; six cards grant or carry indestructible (Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Flawless Maneuver, Immersturm Predator, Mondrak, Glory Dominus, Yahenni, Undying Partisan) and Teferi's Protection phases the whole board out; and eminence rebuilds from a zone no sweeper touches. Still commit in waves — 'redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper' — and note which pieces the insurance does NOT reach: Anointed Procession and Sanguine Bond are enchantments, so only Teferi's Protection and Boros Charm cover them.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: You are the profile the taxes are printed against: 'Decks built on many cheap spells per turn are hit hardest', and 27 of your 64 nonland entries sit at mana value 2 or less. Do the arithmetic the section asks for — 'recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine' — because halving the casts halves the eminence mints and therefore the fodder. Role is forced: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion'. Your outs, enumerated from deck-audit's interaction axis (12 copies): Anguished Unmaking, Despark, Path to Exile, Stroke of Midnight, Winds of Abandon, Boros Charm, Elspeth, Storm Slayer, Liliana, Dreadhorde General, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter, Immersturm Predator, Voldaren Epicure and Altar of Dementia. Breadth covers four of the five classes strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite names — 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any' — with LAND uncovered, so a land-based lock has to be raced rather than answered. Spend the answers on the piece taxing your casts or your life loss, not on the scariest board.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: This is the matchup v1.0.1 improved most, and lifegain is why. Seven printed-lifelink bodies, four makers of 1/1 lifelink Vampire tokens and three granters (all enumerated in the Bloodthirsty Conqueror engine entry) mean your blockers pay you, and with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond on the battlefield every point you gain is a point an opponent loses — defence and offence in one trigger. strategy:life-as-resource: 'Your life total is currency, not a score. Only the last point matters', and 'its points appreciate as they dwindle, so early points are cheap and late points are priceless' — which is the licence for Champion of Dusk, Night's Whisper, Crossway Troublemakers, Bloodtracker and Castle Locthwain to bill you early and the reason to stop paying once a burn or drain seat is live. Do not try to race the whole table: 'you cannot race three life totals — races there are two-player subgames run while the rest of the table develops'. Assign per seat — beatdown against the aggro deck's own life total, blocker-and-drain against the other two.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: You hold no stack interaction, so the levers are the clock, the drain and threat perception. The clock is honestly slow — Forge's median first attack on this list is global turn 13 — the game's own turn counter, roughly your sixth or seventh turn in that run and the 100-game win rate is 0.144 [0.088, 0.228] — so racing a fast kill is not the plan; presenting a drain the table has to answer is. The two verified drain routes (stacks 003, 004/006) are the only lines that end a pod turn on their own, and the single tutor should buy the missing HALF of whichever one is live, per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors: a tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck' and a named card is only '7.1% of your opening seven'. Until you can win, manage perception: 'deploy engines that read as defensive, sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent' — a board of 1/1 tokens and lifelink bodies reads as fair, which is an asset while Bloodthirsty Conqueror or Bloodletter of Aclazotz is still in hand. And prefer the attempt that survives failure: 'Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail'.

distribution_notes: Copies, not entries (deck-facts, decklist sha 7ce22fd6): 100 copies across 96 entries — 36 land copies in 32 entries, 64 spells. Curve (nonland) 12 / 15 / 19 / 8 / 5 / 4 / 1 across mana values 1–7, modal 3, with 27 entries at mana value 2 or less. Roles (coverage 100%, nothing unclassified): threat:body 37, buff:counters 15, sac-outlet 9, sac-cost 9, threat:tokens 9, protection:self 7, draw:engine 6, removal:spot 6, wincon:drain 6, wincon:combat 4, doubler:tokens 3, tutor:unrestricted 1. THE SHAPE MOVED: 15 counter-buff copies and 9 outlets against 9 token-makers is a conversion deck wearing a typal shell, and it is why the archetype budget fits badly — deck-audit reads creatures OVER (37 copies against the aggro band 'aggro 26-32 creatures / 5-6 removal / 34-36 lands' from strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection) and interaction OVER (12 copies against the same band's 5-6), when both counts are deliberate. Mondrak, Glory Dominus is the ONLY non-Vampire creature in the 99, enumerated over all 96 entries. Mana: 36 land copies sits inside the template's '36–38 lands, 10–12 ramp, 10 card draw, 10–12 targeted removal, 3–4 board wipes', but ramp is 8 copies and card draw 7 copies by role against the same line's 10–12 and 10 — with the caveat the section itself supplies, that these are 'counts of *functions*, not cards'; nine further cards draw conditionally (deck-audit possible_uncounted). Colour: 54 black pips across 38 cards (63.5% of the pip load, 42.4% of sources), max 3 pips on one card, against 32 black sources including rocks versus a Karsten target of 36 — strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources, 'his 99-card column assumes 40 lands, on the play, casting on curve, "consistently" ≈ 90%'. On-curve with rocks reads B 85.5%, R 88.1%, W 92.7% (mana_analysis, same sha); 15 of 36 lands enter tapped (42%), and the same section caps 'pure taplands at about four' — three of the 36 are unconditional taplands, the other twelve are shocks and conditionals. Protection is 8 copies against strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's '5-7 protection slots' — deliberately over, because the pivot is the all-in. Bracket floor 4 (Optimized) on three Game Changers (Ancient Tomb, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor) plus the two contained two-card infinites. Goldfish (seed 42, 10,000 iterations, model 7054a07d1a47, max turn 10): keep 80.0% of first sevens, mean 0.24 mulligans, 96.7% can act by turn 3, 91.7% turn-3 land drop, mean available mana 5.59 at turn 6, mean 7.86 bodies at turn 6, mean 1.40 sacrifices by turn 10 and 0.17 by turn 6 — read that last pair as a floor, since the model plays no outlet it has no reason to play. FORGE CANNOT SEE THIS DECK'S NEW PLAN and says so in its own limits: 'Card advantage, tutoring and recursion are ABSENT and cannot be added', and life LOSS that is not damage — every drain in the 99 — 'shows in life_by_turn, eliminated_turn and eliminated_how, never in a damage total'. The 2026-09-02 run is 100 games, which the bench's own rule calls under-powered for a difference of this size. One more hole worth naming: the 28-August pivot asked for a self-mill package as a second dig, and it is NOT in the 99 — Altar of Dementia and Takenuma, Abandoned Mire are the only cards that mill, and Takenuma is the only card in the deck that returns anything from your own graveyard. The synergy graph's 63 intra-deck edges are a format-wide top-10 shortlist, not a per-deck fit score, and contribute nothing to this frame.
overall_assessment: This deck is no longer a critical-mass token deck; it is an ARISTOCRATS deck that happens to make its own fodder for free, and the frame's whole job is to stop the pilot playing the old one. strategy:critical-mass is still the school that names the ignition — 'linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power' — but it also tells you to 'know your number — the count of bodies, spells, or mana at which the deck actually goes over the top', and v1.0.1's number is no longer a body count. It is a count of DEATHS CONVERTED, and nothing in the artifact set measures it: every conversion figure here (outlet 77.6%, death drain 37.2%, draw engine 84.1%) measures a card being DRAWN, never a body being eaten. That is the single largest hole in this deck's evidence and it should be routed to goldfish before anyone reads the conversion stage as green. The reason the pivot is right is strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: '~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan', and the section's own remedy list is what this 99 now runs — 'each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale' — with the corollary that decides which death payoff you deploy first: Cruel Celebrant hits each opponent, Blood Artist hits one target player. The same section supplies the card-selection principle behind the 'enormous vampires, not an army' instruction Alex gave the pilot on 28 August: 'board quality beats board quantity (Walser), because a single scaling permanent out-values a fair board against three players'. Cordial Vampire, Indulgent Aristocrat, Vish Kal and Vampire Socialite are exactly that trade — deaths bought as size — and Forge's 400 games on v1.0.0 are the reason it had to be made. The second axis is cards: the captain's log names 'ran out of steam' and 'no card draw' as the cause on two of four logged games, and strategy:card-advantage is blunt about the stakes — card advantage is 'very likely, the single most important concept in competitive Magic', and in a pod 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'. Sixteen cards in this 99 draw, and the death half of them (Crossway Troublemakers, High-Society Hunter, Liliana, Dreadhorde General, Skullclamp) turns an opponent's removal into your draw step, which is precisely what happened in log entry 004. The third axis is life, and it is now bidirectional: this is a white-black lifegain-into-lifedrain deck, so strategy:life-as-resource's currency framing applies in both directions at once — you pay life for cards with Champion of Dusk, Night's Whisper, Bloodtracker, Crossway Troublemakers and Castle Locthwain, and you convert life gained into life lost with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose and Sanguine Bond. The two contained infinites are the ceiling and not the plan (7.6% assembled, 14.6% with the single tutor); the median game is the drain engine under them, and the pilot's own meta note on 1 September — that losing to a tutored two-card infinite is the unsatisfying kind of loss — is an argument for keeping it that way. What is still unresolved is honest to state: the conversion stage is unmeasured, black is the short colour under 63.5% of the pip load, and the deck's only alternate route (Altar of Dementia) has never been proved.
gaps: No school for ARISTOCRATS: a deck whose own board dying is the payoff has no section. This frame stretched strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's 'resilience instead of restraint' and strategy:card-advantage to cover sacrifice outlets, death triggers and free-outlet density, which is the deck's entire thesis. Wanted: outlet count targets, free-versus-costed outlets, the fodder-to-payoff ratio, and how many payoffs before the outlets are the bottleneck.

No school for TOKENS AS FUEL rather than as threats. strategy:critical-mass prices reaching a threshold of bodies; nothing prices a token whose job is to be eaten, which is the exact distinction the pilot's log entry 003 drew and the reason v1.0.0's 400-game Forge result did not transfer.

No school for LIFEGAIN AS AN ENGINE. strategy:life-as-resource treats life as currency you spend; it has nothing on lifegain as a TRIGGER — lifelink density, gain-to-drain converters, and when a lifegain deck is actually a drain deck. Half this deck's kill routes run through that conversion.

No school for SELF-MILL or the graveyard as a resource: the best query hit scored 0.32 and was about resource denial. The pilot's 28-August pivot explicitly asked for a mill package as a second dig, and there is no theory to check that instinct against — nor any doc line on mill as an alternate win in a pod.
No section on TYPAL DENSITY: lord count against creature count against removal exposure has no target, so the combat layer is sized by measurement alone.

No section on COMMAND-ZONE ENGINES. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance covers the recast tax, which eminence never pays; an ignition that cannot be interacted with, and a commander you often do not want to cast, deserves its own theory.

deck-audit's archetype hint table has no bucket for this deck. The four words it matches on are voltron, combo, control and aggro; 'aristocrats' is none of them, so the frame's archetype string keeps the aggro budget and the audit reads creatures and interaction as OVER when both counts are intentional.
